paper_title: Using the Sun and the Moon as Source masses and the Earth's Rotation as a Modulation to Search for Exotic Spin-Dependent Interactions at Astronomical Distances
coupling_convention: |g_S^N g_P^n| dimensionless scalar(nucleon)-pseudoscalar(neutron) coupling product, exactly as plotted on the y-axis of Fig. 2
notes: Paper derives new limits on exotic spin-dependent interactions using the Sun/Moon as source masses and Earth's rotation as modulation, reanalyzing 3He-129Xe comagnetometer Lorentz-violation data (Allmendinger et al. 2014). Primary result is the monopole-dipole (scalar-pseudoscalar) coupling |g_S^N g_P^n| < 1.6e-35 (95% CL) for interaction range lambda > 1e12 m, valid up to ~1e14 m; encoded as flat bound with mass = hbar*c/lambda (1.97e-7 eV*m / lambda), giving m from ~1.97e-21 eV (lambda=1e14 m) to ~1.97e-19 eV (lambda=1e12 m). Full exclusion extends to lambda ~2e10 m (m ~1e-17 eV) but weaker limits there are only shown in Fig. 2, not tabulated. Paper also constrains VA (|g_V^N g_A^n| < 7.1e-59) and AA (|g_A^N g_A^n| < 8.1e-31) interactions and Hari-Dass alpha1/alpha2 parameters, which are not captured by the MonopoleDipole coupling type. Not a dark matter halo search, so no DM density assumed. | selector: figure_vision over text (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 0, 0.85, 41)) | Vision: Traced FIG. 2 (left plot, page 4): constraint on |g_S^N g_P^n| vs interaction range lambda from 1e6 to 1e14 m. The combined 'this work' boundary is the Moon curve (steep drop at lambda~2e7 m, plateau ~3e-33) for lambda < ~2e10 m and the Sun curve (drop at ~2e10 m, plateau 1.6e-35) for larger lambda. Mass conversion uses m[eV]=1.97e-7/lambda[m], verified against the plot's own top mass axis (10^-14 eV aligns with lambda~2e7 m). Anchored to text values: |g_S g_P| < 1.6e-35 (95% C.L.) for lambda > 1e12 m; Sun curve dominant for lambda > 2e10 m. Boundary shape between anchors follows the exp(-R/lambda)(1/(lambda R)+1/R^2) Yukawa response with R_sun=1.5e11 m and R_moon=3.84e8 m, consistent with the plotted curves. The dashed 'Astro Limit' (SN1987A + WEP) lies slightly below the Moon plateau but is not part of this work's boundary.
